title: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center

place.label: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, Gansu, China
place.basis: One Wikidata (CC0) coordinate for the whole site; a spaceport covers many square kilometres

dates.label: China's first satellite launched from here (CNSA)

facts.text: CNSA says Jiuquan was the first satellite launch site built in China, started in 1958 in the north-east of Jiuquan city, Gansu province.
CNSA says a Long March 1 rocket launched on 24 April 1970 and put China's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, into orbit; it was Jiuquan's first satellite launch.
CNSA says this made China the fifth country able to build and launch its own satellite, after the Soviet Union, the United States, France and Japan.

tiers.everyday: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Gansu, China, was the country's first satellite launch site. China's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, was launched from here on 24 April 1970.
tiers.student: China's space agency says the centre was started in 1958 and covers about 2,800 km². On 24 April 1970 a Long March 1 rocket carried Dongfanghong-1 into orbit, the centre's first satellite launch, which made China the fifth country to launch its own satellite.
